official_sources: Creating a design code coding process

official_measurement_examples.name: National Design Guide characteristics
official_measurement_examples.fact: The National Design Guide uses 10 characteristics of well-designed places.

official_measurement_examples.name: Design-code process steps
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current creating-a-design-code guidance describes seven steps spanning analysis, vision, code and delivery activities.

official_measurement_examples.name: Design review semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Practice Guidance describes design review as independent multidisciplinary advice and says it does not replace statutory consultee advice or local authority design skills.

official_measurement_examples.name: Design-code data model
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data specifies separate design-code and design-code-area datasets, which may also be combined through geometry fields.

official_measurement_examples.name: Office for Place 10 criteria status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 10 criteria page explicitly says the criteria are good-practice material and do not constitute government planning policy or guidance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Design consultation status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The January 2026 Design and Placemaking Planning Practice Guidance publication is a consultation on draft consolidated guidance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Masterplan role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Design-code guidance says a masterplan can establish street networks, area types and parameters for larger allocated development sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local design requirements
official_measurement_examples.fact: The LURA design-code provisions require development-plan design requirements to be prepared for areas, but the existence of a code does not itself grant permission.

core_rules: National Design Guide is guidance not planning permission
National Model Design Code is guidance not a parcel code
local design code is not planning permission
design-code area is not a Land Registry title boundary
design-code intersection is not automatic refusal
design-code compliance is not automatic permission
design-code noncompliance requires planning judgement and policy context
design guide and design code must not be treated as identical instruments
design review advice is not the LPA decision
design review is not statutory-consultee approval
positive design review is not planning permission
negative design review is not planning refusal
pre-application design advice is not a formal decision
Design and Access Statement is not planning approval
masterplan is not planning permission
allocated-site masterplan is not proof all parameters are approved
coding plan is not an ownership plan
area type is not a cadastral classification
national design characteristic is not a parcel score
context assessment must not be fabricated from generic map proximity
identity judgement must not be reduced to a binary flag without evidence
built-form quality is not inferred from density alone
movement design is distinct from transport-capacity evidence
nature design is distinct from BNG compliance
public-space design is distinct from public ownership
use mix is not evidence of lawful use
building design quality is distinct from Building Regulations compliance
resource-efficiency design is not EPC certification
lifespan guidance is not a structural-life warranty
numerical design parameter must retain the code and geography that created it
illustrative NMDC dimensions are not universal mandatory dimensions
local code must be date-scoped to adoption or publication status
draft design code is not adopted policy
consultation response is not adopted code
community preference evidence is not planning permission
developer-prepared code is not adopted local policy unless formally given weight
Office for Place 10 criteria are good practice not government policy
design consultation draft must not override current adopted guidance
Planning Data dataset is not guaranteed complete legal coverage
data-format compliance is not policy compliance
design-code dataset reference is not a site permission identifier
design review recommendation implementation must be evidenced separately
post-permission design quality checks are not new planning permission
condition discharge must not be inferred from design conformity
amended scheme must be checked against the actual approved plans
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no design requirement
no parcel design approval or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research confidence is not parcel design accuracy
